findings.impact: HTTP connections made by Android framework components are not rejected by the manifest policy.
findings.limit: This does not prove that a particular login or update request uses HTTP. The native connector has its own TLS implementation.
findings.title: Application permits cleartext traffic

evidence: QPlayActivity is explicitly exported and accepts graalclassic:// and graalclassicplus://.
OnCreate passes the Intent action and URI string to OnIntent, which posts OnDeepLink to Natives.onInvokeEvent.
findings.impact: Any installed application can request the exported scheme. The native event handler must treat action, URI, and extras as untrusted input.
findings.limit: No malicious caller or server payload was used in this audit.
findings.title: Exported custom-scheme activity reaches native deep-link handling

findings.confidence: confirmed capability, reachability depends on page source
evidence: classes2.dex contains WebTop, setJavaScriptEnabled, and addJavascriptInterface.
The bridge exposes getAndroidId, getSZ, loadData, message, and saveData.
messageGui builds a quoted JavaScript call by concatenating id and data without escaping.
findings.impact: A page that can reach the bridge can read device and persistent state, write preferences, and send messages into native dispatch. Unescaped messageGui data is a JavaScript injection sink if attacker-controlled data reaches it.
findings.limit: The recovered WebTop URL was not opened, and this report does not claim that a remote page can reach every bridge method in a production run.
findings.title: WebTop enables JavaScript and exposes a native JavaScript bridge

findings.confidence: confirmed capability, reachability depends on command source
evidence: WebTop recognizes load_dex and java_reflection commands.
iDex writes webview_injected_<id>.dex under the app files directory, creates a DexClassLoader, and invokes a reflected Context method.
findings.impact: If an untrusted page or message source can supply these commands, it creates an in-process code-loading boundary with access to the app's permissions and data.
findings.limit: The audit did not inject DEX, invoke reflection, or contact the recovered WebTop URL.
findings.title: WebTop can write DEX bytes and load classes reflectively

findings.confidence: confirmed embedded legacy material, active trust use unproven
evidence: res/raw/fabzat_com.crt is a PEM certificate for admin.fabzat.com.
Validity ends at 2014-08-23T05:22:41 and the signature hash is sha1.
findings.impact: Any code that treats this file as a trust anchor or pins it cannot validate a current service certificate after expiry.
findings.limit: The file's presence does not prove that current startup or login consumes it.
findings.title: APK embeds an expired SHA-1 Fabzat certificate

findings.confidence: confirmed legacy vocabulary, active suite selection unproven
evidence: ARM64 libqplay.so contains TLSv1.1, TLSv1.2, RC4, and NULL cipher suite names.
The library uses a bundled CyaSSL implementation rather than Android's Java trust stack.
findings.impact: Legacy protocol support expands downgrade and configuration risk if those suites are enabled by the connector path.
findings.limit: String presence alone does not show that a weak suite was negotiated. Existing loopback evidence preserved peer and hostname verification.
findings.title: Native qplay contains legacy TLS and weak cipher identifiers

findings.confidence: confirmed embedded bundle, active validation path separately reviewed
evidence: The ARM64 qplay library contains the 12,820-byte trust text also found in the 1.8 library.
The repository's CyaSSL review decodes six historical certificate blocks; the earliest recorded leaf expired in 2023.
findings.impact: A connector path that still validates against this fixed bundle can fail against a renewed service chain or require an unsafe verification bypass.
findings.limit: This audit did not contact a live service and does not claim that every Spectron connection enables this trust path.
findings.title: Spectron carries the historical native connector trust bundle

evidence: libxposed.so imports dlopen, dlsym, and mprotect and contains A64_HOOK and inline-hook strings.
IDA review mapped crash, freeze, and abort branches in Java_com_WebTop_onmsg; load_menu, setscript, and gs2call forward modding payloads.
findings.impact: The mod layer can alter qplay behavior and deliberately terminate or hang the process. It is a separate trust boundary from the old connector.
findings.limit: This finding describes the supplied modded APK and is not attributed to the original 1.8 package.
findings.severity: critical stability and integrity risk in the supplied mod
findings.title: Bundled libxposed installs hooks and contains destructive WebTop commands

evidence: readelf reports RW GNU_STACK for the packaged native libraries.
The qplay and xposed libraries also contain GNU_RELRO and BIND_NOW metadata.
findings.impact: These are useful exploit mitigations, although they do not compensate for unsafe input or code-loading paths.
findings.limit: The report does not claim full RELRO or complete runtime hardening.
findings.title: Native libraries have non-executable GNU_STACK segments
